agent_internal_notes: User uploaded a PNG whiteboard photo. Got 'processing failed' error. Had them retry and it worked on second attempt. Seemed like a transient timeout.

Customer asked why their January invoice was $400 higher than expected. Had to check Salesforce for contract tier, then admin portal for seat count, then billing dashboard. Took me 25 min just to gather the info before I could even start responding.
Canvas lagging with 200+ objects. Recommended splitting into pages. Quick fix.

Import of a 30-page PDF produced messy layout. Told user to wait for Design Curation review. Customer said 'this is the third time this week I've had to wait — my team is losing patience.' Enterprise account (Meridian Health, 450 seats).
New enterprise onboarding — 80 users can't access workspace. SSO config issue. Had to escalate to engineering Slack channel. No response for 3.5 hours. Customer CEO emailed our CEO directly.
Spreadsheet import failed. User retried and it worked. Same transient error pattern as T-4801.

Customer wants refund for unused seats. Policy says no mid-cycle refunds, but I had to check three places to confirm: the Google Sheet policy doc, the admin portal, and Salesforce. Policy sheet was last updated in November — not sure if it's current.
Another processing timeout on image upload. Third one today. User frustrated — said 'does this feature actually work?' Told them to retry. It worked. We should probably be tracking these.
User wants dark mode. Sent to feature request form. Easy.

Enterprise customer (Luma Analytics, 200 seats) wants to downgrade. VP of Product there says 'Magic Import quality has degraded significantly since we onboarded 4 months ago.' I flagged in #customer-health but no one responded. This feels like churn risk not just a support ticket.

User uploaded architectural blueprints. AI output was unusable — misidentified structural elements as text. Routed to Design Curation. Queue shows 67 hour wait. Told customer 2-3 hours per our SLA. That's not going to happen.
Real-time cursors not syncing between users. Had them clear cache and rejoin. Worked. Known intermittent issue per eng but no public status page or internal knowledge article about it.

Enterprise SSO broken for entire org (CoreVista, 300 seats). Tier 2 not available — no one staffed after 6pm EST. Left in queue. Picked back up at 9am next day. Customer lost an entire evening of work across their team.
PDF import failed. Retry worked. I used Sarah's workaround macro to send the 'please retry' message — saves a lot of typing since we send this 15+ times per day.

Came in overnight. No one picked it up until morning. Customer had replied twice asking for an update before we even opened it. Enterprise account (DataForge, 175 seats). James noted: 'email tickets from enterprise accounts shouldn't sit overnight but we have no way to flag them automatically.'
Handwritten notes scan came out garbled. Routed to Curation. Customer asked for ETA — I said 2-3 hours. Actual queue is now 70+ hours. I don't feel good about this.
Password reset. Quick resolution. Voice channel works well for these.
Image import timeout. Retry fixed it. Fourth day in a row we're seeing this pattern during morning hours. Possibly related to batch processing load?

Customer needs Jira integration support. Our docs are outdated — still reference v1 API. I had to ping engineering in Slack to get current setup instructions. Took 2 hours to get a response. We need updated KB articles badly.

Customer charged twice for same billing period. I found the duplicate in admin portal but can't issue refunds from there — had to go to Stripe dashboard, then back to Salesforce to log it, then email Finance team for approval. Four systems to fix one billing error. Customer was furious. This has happened 3 times this month.
Transient import failure on CSV upload. Retry resolved. I've started keeping a personal tally — this is the 23rd retry-resolved import error I've handled this week.
Slow load time. User on older browser. Recommended Chrome update. Resolved.

New enterprise customer (NovaTech, 500 seats) onboarding. SSO, custom domain, and data residency requirements. No runbook exists for complex onboarding. I had to coordinate across 4 Slack channels and 3 teams over 2 days. Customer's IT director said 'this is the most disorganized onboarding we've ever experienced.'

Complex flowchart PDF. AI completely mangled the connector lines and label positioning. Customer is a design lead at Meridian Health (same enterprise from T-4804). Said 'if this isn't fixed by Friday, I'm recommending we switch to Miro.' Second complaint from this account in 2 days.
Wants keyboard shortcuts for alignment. Logged in feature tracker.

User called about repeated import failures. Talked them through it on the call — it was a file size issue (>50MB). Our error message just says 'processing failed' with no mention of size limits. User said 'your error messages are useless.' They're right.

Customer asking about annual vs monthly pricing for upgrade. Had to check Salesforce for their current contract, then the Google Sheet pricing matrix, then confirm with Sales in Slack. Three sources for pricing info that should be in one place.

DataForge (175 seats, same account from T-4815) submitting cancellation request. Reason: 'poor support responsiveness and Magic Import quality regression.' This is the third enterprise cancellation request this month citing the same two reasons.

After-hours SSO emergency. Same pattern as T-4813 — no Tier 2 coverage after 6pm. Customer (Ridgeline Corp, 250 seats) locked out during a client presentation. Devon noted: 'This is the second after-hours SSO emergency this week. We are going to lose enterprise customers over this.'
Import timeout. Retry worked. Evening shift, lighter load — still happening though. Maybe not just a load issue.
